title: Blank conditions: what an entity does whose circuit condition is in use and has no first signal, next to conditions that hold and that do not
source: Recorded from the game by tools/game-probe/blank-condition.mjs: the control behaviours of the runtime API (circuit_condition with its `fulfilled`, LuaGenericOnOffControlBehavior.disabled), LuaEntity.status, and LuaItemStack.import_stack, build_blueprint and create_blueprint.
layout: cases: per prototype the switch of its condition in a blueprint (flag; a speaker has none) and its readings after `ticks` ticks next to a constant combinator that sends `signal` = 1. state: blank (switch on, no condition written), blank-unwired (the same without a wire), true (signal > 0), false (signal < 0), false-unwired (the same without a wire), off (switch off, signal < 0), blank-equals-zero (no first signal, = 0: holds if a blank signal reads as 0). built: how the entity was made, from a blueprint string with the entity, the combinator and the wire (blueprint) or through the runtime API (api); one reading for both where they say the same. wires: red wires on the entity. signal: what it reads of `signal` on red. controlBehavior: whether it has one. flag and condition: as the control behaviour gives them back, fulfilled being the game's `fulfilled` of that condition. disabled: LuaGenericOnOffControlBehavior.disabled. status: LuaEntity.status by its name in defines.entity_status. active, disabledByControlBehavior: the attributes of LuaEntity. itemFrom, itemTo: an item on a belt, as its distance to the end of the line when it was put there and at the end (0: carried to the end). switchOn: LuaEntity.power_switch_state. gateOpened: is_opened of the gate next to a wall. signalState: LuaEntity.signal_state by name. unavailable: reads the entity does not have. exported: its control_behavior in a blueprint the game makes of it, null where it writes none. error: what the game refused. deciders: decider combinators that send signal-B = 1 when their conditions hold and signal-C = 1 when they do not, with the conditions as the game gives them back, what they read of `signal` on red and what they sent in the last tick; empty has no condition, blank-above-minus-one and blank-below-signal hold if a blank signal reads as 0.
